_provenance: Canonical normalized model over already-real Project 1 sources - no product, paper, signal, competitor, cluster, pattern, or relationship is invented here. All 7 evidence families (PRODUCTS/RESEARCH/CONSUMERS/TRENDS/MARKET/RIVALS/TECHNOLOGY_AI) stay explicitly separate. HDBSCAN/BERTopic-style clustering is deliberately NOT used anywhere - every current family is small (<100 real items), and DATA_FABRIC.md's own acceptance criteria require small-corpus clustering not be forced into a large-corpus method.

evidence_objects.title: Real-World Effectiveness of Portable Air Cleaners in Reducing Home Particulate Matter Concentrations

payload.question: Does a portable air cleaner's benefit reach rooms beyond the one it sits in?
payload.found: PM2.5/PM10 fell 78.8%/63.9% in the primary room and 57.9%/60.4% in a secondary room during the filter condition vs. sham.
payload.establishes: A single PAC measurably reduces PM in the room it occupies and, to a lesser degree, an adjacent room, especially with a central air handler running.
payload.does_not_establish: That secondary-room reduction generalizes to homes without central air handling, or to non-COVID-positive households.

evidence_objects.title: Reduction of personal PM2.5 exposure via indoor air filtration systems in Detroit: an intervention study

payload.question: Do cheaper HEPA-type filters reduce personal PM2.5 exposure nearly as well as true-HEPA?
payload.found: True-HEPA cut personal PM2.5 exposure 53% and indoor concentration 60%; a cheaper HEPA-type filter still cut exposure 31% and concentration 52%.
payload.establishes: Both high- and low-efficiency portable filtration measurably reduce personal PM2.5 exposure for older adults, not just indoor air readings.
payload.does_not_establish: That the gap between true-HEPA and HEPA-type performance is negligible for all pollutant sizes or health outcomes.

evidence_objects.title: Effectiveness of portable HEPA air cleaners on reducing indoor PM2.5 and NH3 in an agricultural cohort of children with asthma: A randomized intervention trial

payload.question: Do HEPA cleaners lower both PM2.5 and ammonia in farmworker children's homes with asthma?
payload.found: HEPA homes had 60% lower sleeping-area and 42% lower living-area PM2.5 at one year; ammonia reductions were not observed.
payload.establishes: Sustained (one-year) PM2.5 reduction is achievable with two placed units in real agricultural-community homes.
payload.does_not_establish: That reduced PM2.5 translated into fewer asthma symptoms - no clinical/symptom endpoint was reported in this result.

evidence_objects.title: PM10, PM2.5, PM1, and PM0.1 resuspension due to human walking

payload.question: How much does ordinary walking resuspend settled particles back into room air?
payload.found: 10 minutes of walking measurably raised PM10/PM2.5/PM1/PM0.1 concentrations, with estimated resuspension rates reported per size fraction.
payload.establishes: Human movement over a loaded carpet is a real, measurable indoor particle source, not just deposition.
payload.does_not_establish: That a floor-level or mobile purifier would outperform a conventional room-level purifier - this study did not test any purifier placement.

evidence_objects.title: Self-reported health impacts of do-it-yourself air cleaner use in a smoke-impacted community

payload.question: Does using a low-cost DIY air cleaner during smoke events change self-reported symptoms?
payload.found: No association was found between DIY air-cleaner usage and self-reported symptoms; usage itself was low, and loud operating noise was cited as a barrier to use.
payload.establishes: In this small pilot, noise was a real, named reason people ran the device less than intended.
payload.does_not_establish: That air cleaners don't help symptoms in general - the sample was too small and usage too inconsistent to draw a causal conclusion either way.

evidence_objects.title: Analysis of sources and sinks of indoor particulate matter reveals insights into the real-world efficacy of portable air cleaners in a randomized intervention trial

payload.question: Do simple before/after PM averages correctly show whether a portable air cleaner is working?
payload.found: Raw averages misleadingly showed higher PM in the active-filtration group (higher source strength homes); background-period PM was ~36% lower with active filtration, and loss rates rose ~15-130% with fan speed.
payload.establishes: Fan-speed-dependent loss rates, not raw before/after averages, are the credible way to show PAC efficacy in an unbalanced real-home sample.
payload.does_not_establish: That every home in the active group experienced the same benefit - source-strength imbalance between groups means simple averages cannot be trusted.

evidence_objects.title: The impact of portable air cleaners on indoor particulate matter concentrations and perceptions of indoor air quality: a randomized crossover trial in three multifamily buildings

payload.question: Does automatic (threshold-triggered) operation clean as well as running a purifier constantly?
payload.found: Constant operation cut weekly mean PM2.5 by 66% (95% CI 59-72%); auto operation cut it by 40% (95% CI 27-50%) but sharply reduced runtime.
payload.establishes: Auto mode trades measurable filtration effectiveness for much less runtime; measured performance diverged from theoretical CADR-based sizing.
payload.does_not_establish: That one control strategy (always-constant or always-auto) is optimal for every home - the paper explicitly says a universal strategy may not fit.

evidence_objects.title: Indoor environmental health and asthma relief: findings from a longitudinal HEPA filter trial

payload.question: Does 8 months of real HEPA H14 filtration measurably improve asthma control, not just air readings?
payload.found: The active group gained +2.2 Asthma Control Test points and +27.7% symptom-free days versus placebo, alongside a 29.6 microg/m3 PM2.5 drop (all p<=0.004).
payload.establishes: In this one RCT, sustained HEPA H14 filtration is associated with a measurable clinical asthma-control benefit, not only an air-quality change.
payload.does_not_establish: That this specific effect size generalizes beyond this single trial - treat as a candidate finding requiring independent replication before treating as settled.

evidence_objects.title: Low-cost sensors for indoor air quality monitoring: A systematic review of accuracy, applications, and limitations

payload.question: How accurate are the low-cost sensors that consumer air purifiers use to sense and react?
payload.found: Many low-cost sensors correlate well with reference instruments under controlled conditions, but performance varies significantly with humidity, temperature, and pollutant source; most devices don't yet meet formal regulatory validation standards.
payload.establishes: Low-cost PM/CO2 sensing is workable for consumer devices but context-dependent, and current products largely lack standardized validation.
payload.does_not_establish: That any specific consumer purifier's onboard sensor is accurate enough to safely drive fully autonomous decisions in all conditions.

evidence_objects.title: Validating the performance of low-cost IAQ sensors through co-location

payload.question: When two consumer-grade IAQ sensors are placed next to lab-grade references, how well do they agree?
payload.found: One consumer sensor tracked relative CO2/PM changes well (higher correlation) but showed higher bias/RMSE (lower absolute accuracy) than the reference; averaging over longer intervals improved but did not eliminate the gap.
payload.establishes: A consumer sensor can be precise (consistent, good for trends) while still being inaccurate (wrong absolute number) at the same time - these are different properties.
payload.does_not_establish: That either tested sensor is reliable enough for uncalibrated absolute-concentration claims without in-situ calibration.

evidence_objects.title: Toward Better and Healthier Air Quality: Global PM2.5 and O3 Pollution Status and Risk Assessment Based on the New WHO Air Quality Guidelines for 2021

payload.question: Against the WHO's tightened 2021 PM2.5/O3 guideline, how much of the world's urban population still lives with unhealthy ambient air, and where?
payload.found: Across 618 cities (2019-2022), only ~10% of days globally met the new WHO PM2.5 guideline (<=15 ug/m3); over 35% of cities show compound PM2.5-O3 pollution; exposure-risk categories are markedly worse for cities in China/India than for economically developed cities.
payload.establishes: Ambient/outdoor PM2.5 exposure against the tightened 2021 WHO guideline remains widespread globally - a demand-context fact (a large population is still exposed to guideline-exceeding outdoor air), not a claim about any indoor air cleaner's effectiveness.
payload.does_not_establish: Anything about portable/indoor air cleaner performance, sales, or consumer behaviour - this is outdoor ambient monitoring-station data only, with no purifier or indoor-environment measurement.

evidence_objects.title: A Burning Issue: Wildfire Smoke Exposure, Retail Sales, and Demand for Adaptation in Healthcare

payload.question: When wildfire smoke hits an area, does that show up as a genuine, measurable bump in real retail demand for air purifiers - and how long does it last?
payload.found: Wildfire smoke exposure increases retail sales of air purifiers, bottled water, and cold/cough/nasal remedies, with a documented lagged effect (smoke from prior weeks still elevates current-week sales).
payload.establishes: A review-volume or sales burst coinciding with a wildfire event is a genuine, external-shock-driven demand signal, not a data anomaly to discount by default - directly relevant to how this project's own burst-detection judgment calls should treat wildfire-coincident spikes.
payload.does_not_establish: Anything about product performance, review sentiment, or which brand/features people bought - this is an aggregate sales-volume study, not a product-quality or preference study.

lineage_edges.relation_basis: Randomized controlled trial - randomized design supports a causal estimate.
Randomized intervention trial - randomized design supports a causal estimate.
Small pilot phased-intervention study (n=10) - underpowered/uncontrolled enough to be a hypothesis, not a settled estimate.
Small pilot phased-intervention study (n=10) - underpowered/uncontrolled enough to be a hypothesis, not a settled estimate.
Three-arm randomized crossover trial - randomized design supports a causal estimate.
Single-blinded randomized cross-over intervention - randomized design supports a causal estimate.
Double-blinded randomized crossover intervention - randomized design supports a causal estimate.
Randomized parallel-group intervention trial - randomized design supports a causal estimate.
Three-arm randomized crossover trial - randomized design supports a causal estimate.
PRISMA systematic review of accuracy studies - synthesizes real empirical associations, does not itself run a new causal test.
Co-location validation explicitly reports Pearson correlation between sensor and reference instrument.
Three-arm randomized crossover trial - randomized design supports a causal estimate.
Controlled full-scale laboratory chamber experiment - controlled manipulation supports a causal estimate.
